claim: An instruction registers only if its own checker rejects the violating fixture it ships and accepts the satisfying one — a checker that cannot discriminate between them is refused.

steps.label: a checker that tells the two fixtures apart
steps.evidence: the fixtures stay attached, so the claim can be re-verified rather than trusted

steps.label: a checker that passes everything
steps.detail: INS-011 passes an artifact it is supposed to reject
steps.note: A policy full of checkers that never fire reports total compliance and means nothing.

steps.label: a checker that fails everything
steps.detail: INS-012 fails an artifact it is supposed to accept
steps.note: Not vacuous, useless in the other direction: it would fail every artifact and be switched off within a day.

steps.label: a checker looking for the wrong string
steps.detail: INS-013 passes an artifact it is supposed to reject
steps.note: The real shape of this bug. Without a violating fixture it passes every artifact forever, silently, and looks exactly like a checker that works.

steps.label: an instruction shipped without a violating fixture
steps.note: Without one there is no way to tell a strict checker from a stub.

steps.label: a checker that raises on its own fixture
steps.detail: INS-016 raised RuntimeError on its violating fixture

steps.label: what a registry ends up holding
steps.evidence: only the falsifiable one was admitted
